introduction: An oblique orbital photograph turns a vast Andean landscape into an almost abstract field of ridges and basins.
observe: Look for overlapping ridgelines that reveal depth.
Notice how little in the frame provides an immediate human scale.
explanation: This is the Altiplano of the Andes in South America, photographed from orbit. Perspective compresses distant landforms and makes elevation easier to read than absolute size.
colorMethod: The colors come from reflected visible light recorded photographically; atmosphere, viewing angle and surface materials affect their appearance.
whyItMatters: Planetary landscapes can look familiar at first glance. Shape, context and scale are stronger evidence than resemblance alone.
